subject.title: Google Chat: agent-to-agent (bot↔bot) conversation doesn't work — a Chat app doesn't receive messages from another Chat app (same setup works on Discord)

question: Should OpenClaw treat Google Chat app-to-app multi-agent conversations as a documented channel limitation for now, or sponsor an opt-in channel-independent A2A bridge?
rationale: The source path can document the limitation, but automatic bridging would create new cross-agent delivery semantics beyond the current Google Chat plugin behavior.

options.title: Document Limitation Now
options.body: Add a Google Chat and multi-agent docs warning that `allowBots` only applies after a delivered bot-authored event, then track any bridge separately.

options.title: Sponsor A2A Bridge Design
options.body: Define an opt-in bridge around existing sessions_send and agentToAgent policy before implementation or repair automation starts.

options.title: Declare Unsupported
options.body: Close after a maintainer decision that Google Chat app-to-app autonomous conversations are not planned beyond explicit sessions_send usage.

recommendation.title: Document Limitation Now
recommendation.body: Add a Google Chat and multi-agent docs warning that `allowBots` only applies after a delivered bot-authored event, then track any bridge separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses bot-loop protection and multi-agent routing, both areas with strong history from this owner signal.
